paragraphs: Rabbi Yose of Dormaskit: the Targum renders Damascus as Dormaskit. He expounded in Sifrei, beginning of Devarim, and Shir HaShirim Rabbah, on ‘Your neck is like an ivory tower,’ that Jerusalem’s gates will one day reach Damascus. He told Rabbi Yehudah: ‘I am from Damascus, and there is a place there named Chadrach’; see there and Yalkut, Zechariah, section 9. Chagigah 3b: Rabbi Yose ben Dormaskit. Likewise Kiddushin 39a: Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Yose says in Rabbi Yose ben Dormaskit’s name, who spoke in Rabbi Yose HaGelili’s name. In Shocher Tov, section 25, and Sifra, several times. In Devarim, cited above, Rabbi Yose ben Dormaskit told Rabbi Yehudah Berabbi: ‘Why do you distort the Scriptures against us?’ and so forth. Megillah 7a: Rabbi Eliezer says, Rabbi Akiva says, Rabbi Meir says, Rabbi Yose ben Dormaskit says. Bereshit Rabbah, section 32, and Chullin 67b. It appears that Dormaskit was his father’s name, rather than a place-name. He was present on the day they appointed Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah Nasi, and came to learn with Rabbi Eliezer the Great; see his entry. He told him they had agreed that Ammon and Moab give the poor tithe in the seventh year. He said it was a law to Moses from Sinai: ‘God’s secret is for those who fear Him,’ as in Mishnah, Yadayim 4:3. In Chagigah 3b Rabbi Eliezer grew angry with him; his eyes came out, and he caught them in his hand. Afterwards he was reconciled with him, prayed for him, and his eyes returned to their place.
